contexts.text: Moses was feeding the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian () = that the Law from the Divine was instructing those who were in the truth of simple good.

Father-in-law = the good from which as from a father comes forth that good which is conjoined with truth... The quality of this good is Jethro. The priest of Midian = the good of the Church where are those who are in the truth of simple good.
Jethro his father-in-law = the good of the Church which is in the truth of simple good.

To Jethro his father-in-law () = in simple good; namely, what is continuous of life. (For) Jethro, being the priest of Midian, = the good of the Church which is in the truth of simple good. This good is meant by simple good.
The good Divine, from which is the ordination, is represented (in ) by Jethro the father-in-law of Moses.

And Jethro the priest of Midian heard () = Divine good. (For) Jethro the priest of Midian represents the good of the Church which is in the truth of simple good; but here, Divine good, because Moses, whose father-in-law he was, represented Divine truth... The reason Divine good is here represented by Jethro, is that it treats in this chapter of the ordination of truths with the man of the Spiritual Church, which is effected by Divine good through Divine truth; for all ordination is by good through truth.
Jethro the father-in-law of Moses represents Divine good. AC 8654. AC 8657. AC 8661. AC 8662. AC 8688. AC 8697. AC 8724.
Jethro rejoiced over all the good which Jehovah had done to Israel () = the state of Divine good when all things succeed.
By Jethro is represented Divine good united to Divine truth, which is represented by Moses.
This turning or change of one state into another is what is described in this chapter by Jethro.
For Jethro represented the Divine good, thus the Divine Itself.
